hot.title: VideoJev: System One Model for Video Understanding and Interaction
hot.summary: VideoJev scores candidate time intervals to locate events and candidate answers for video questions, reusing one video prefix across queries through cached or joint inference. It reports 65.3 mean temporal intersection-over-union, versus 58.6 for its 4B backbone, and a four-benchmark QA mean of 74.3, near 74.9 for Qwen3.5-4B Thinking; evaluations cover grounding and multiple-choice QA, not agent workflows.

hot.title: Hybrid Reasoning Agents
hot.summary: HybridAgent lets a tool-using language-model agent reason in continuous hidden states and use text for tool calls and answers. HybridLink aligns hidden states with the model’s input-embedding space, while retained attention-cache entries carry context across turns. At 14B parameters, it scores 49.5 average on WebWalker versus ARPO’s 40.5, within evaluations of Qwen3-Base models on 11 benchmarks.

hot.title: Towards Agentic Robots: Model, Data, Environment, and Harness
hot.summary: The authors survey agentic robots as systems that use goals, observations, capabilities, and execution feedback to choose actions, gather information, revise plans, or recover. They organize prior work into four domains and seventeen overlapping categories. An external RoboDojo evaluation reports 22.48% average success across 42 simulation tasks, versus 19.34% for trained DM0.5; this comparison does not isolate feedback’s effect.

hot.title: Correction Training for Diffusion Models
hot.summary: The authors introduce a corrector for diffusion image generation that refines the denoiser’s clean-image prediction before each sampling update. Trained on the denoiser’s own predictions, the corrector can be applied repeatedly. On class-conditional ImageNet-256 with DiT-XL/2 at 250 network evaluations, it lowers FID-50K from 9.58 unguided to 2.07, versus 2.51 for CFG, with lower precision but higher recall than CFG.

hot.title: Scalable Weak-to-Strong Verifier Hardening for Agent Environments
hot.summary: The authors introduce an executable-verifier hardening method combining an isolated sandbox with an online hacker–fixer loop. The hacker searches with verifier-source access; the fixer repairs checks, then tests legitimate solutions. On 102 selected Terminal Bench tasks, Opus 5’s unhinted per-trial attack success rate fell from 69.9% to 12.1%, while benign solve rate changed from 93.1% to 91.2%; this does not establish that all vulnerabilities are closed.

hot.title: RoboSimStudio: An Interactive Toolkit for Human and Agent Rapid Real2Sim of Robot Manipulation Tasks
hot.summary: RoboSimStudio provides an interactive simulation workflow for robot manipulation, where humans and coding agents can inspect and edit solvers, contact models, and material parameters. In a smartphone-video-based sponge-wiping pilot, its simulation feedback supported policy improvement from 0% to 100% reported simulated wiped-area progress by iteration 14. The policy completed a real wipe, but another rollout failed after a bar support moved.

hot.title: Interaction-as-a-Judge
hot.summary: The authors introduce interaction-based evaluation: a computer-use agent operates an app, and a judge assesses the resulting trace. Gemini 3 Flash reaches 69.1% accuracy on pairwise preferences, versus 65.6% with code alone. GPT 5.6 Sol reaches 81.6% on requirement verification, versus 77.0%. Interaction feedback also repairs more initially broken requirements within five iterations, while requirement discovery remains difficult.

hot.title: Cowork-Gym: Synthesizing Interactive Work Environments at Scale
hot.summary: Cowork-Gym generates environments for agents working with people through shared files and tools. It builds tasks, workspaces, user policies, and hybrid checks, then runs and revises environments; simulated users respond to progress and can change inputs. Qwen models improve in most comparisons; Ours-27B scores 0.8400 on PawBench under OpenClaw, but WildClawBench is a weakness and the pool is not representative.

hot.title: Jeva: System One Models from First Principles
hot.summary: Jeva decides among candidate sets by separately encoding requests and options, then refining the request state against reusable option representations. Its decision head supports set-conditioned comparisons and an explicit null outcome; option computation can be reused across requests. On long-document sets with complete option reuse, hybrid caching reduced median latency from 2,102.0 ms to 75.1 ms, a 27.98× speedup.

hot.title: LatentLoop: Scaling Looped MoE Models with Asymmetric Compute Allocation
hot.summary: LatentLoop reallocates computation in looped MoE models by compressing the sequence for the first visit, writing its update back to full resolution, and processing the full sequence on the second visit. Across 15 matched configurations, it has lower validation negative log-likelihood than baselines. Fitted curves predict 19.0% and 7.9% less training computation at equal loss, within the observed allocation range.

hot.title: LLM-to-Flow Distillation: Teaching Natural Language Goals to Scientific Generators
hot.summary: LFD adapts a flow generator to natural-language scientific goals by having a frozen LLM propose attainable sub-goals and judge sampled candidates, then training on positive-versus-negative preferences. It repeats this process as the generator changes. In GSK3β ATP-pocket design, LFD reached a mean GNINA CNNaffinity of 6.77 ± 0.11 pK, above reward-guided baselines; this is computational docking evidence, not experimental validation.

hot.title: Any Time, Any Space: A World-State-Centric Framework for Agentic Video Generation
hot.summary: ATAS addresses screenplay-to-video continuity by storing static scene geometry and time-indexed event evidence for later shots. Validation separates film inclusion from memory updates. ATAS reports 15.968 PSNR_C on spatial revisit, versus ViewCrafter’s 15.255, and leads three event-recapture axes but trails ReCA on action-and-state preservation; event tests use no synchronized target video.

hot.title: CyberArena: Benchmarking AI Agents in Live Symmetric Attack-and-Defense Combat
hot.summary: CyberArena evaluates cybersecurity agents in reciprocal contests: two agents attack and patch identical vulnerable services over three rounds, and defensive changes persist. A latent-ability model adjusts scores for opponents and challenges. On 30 challenges all three comparison models solved solo, round-three capture rates were 52%, 37%, and 35%; these rates do not establish patching as the sole cause.

hot.title: Mitigating Cross-Modal Hallucinations by Correcting Modality Misrouting in Omnimodal LLMs
hot.summary: CaRe addresses audio-visual errors where a correct modality-specific answer is lost in the joint prediction. A text-only probe nominates audio or video; if the unimodal and joint answers disagree, CaRe steers the joint representation toward the unimodal reference while retaining both modalities. On CMM, MiniCPM-o-2.6 reaches 86.9% accuracy versus MAD’s 77.3%; evidence is limited to discrete-answer cross-modal hallucination benchmarks.

hot.title: DuoDiscover: Scaling Autonomous Discovery Beyond the Evaluation Bottleneck
hot.summary: DuoDiscover searches for code regions to optimize while building a target-specific, inexpensive evaluator for ranking edits. Workers explore with these yardsticks, test their rankings against full evaluations, and use full evaluations to confirm gains. In a 20-hour, four-agent vLLM comparison, it achieved a 1.92× geometric-mean gain versus 1.07× for Claude Code, a result limited to this setup.

hot.title: ForceWAM: Decoupling Future and Response Learning from Demo and Play Data for Contact-Rich Manipulation
hot.summary: ForceWAM predicts future wrist-camera images and force/torque trajectories for a task, while learning action responses from successful demonstrations and exploratory play. It updates actions using measured wrench feedback between slower future updates. In force-regulated sliding, it achieves 85% success, versus 40% with task-only training and 20% for the strongest external baselines. Rates span 85% to 95% across four tested conditions.

hot.title: HarnessTTT: Learn to Optimize Harness at Test-Time for Scientific Discovery
hot.summary: HarnessTTT trains a proposer to write executable harnesses that guide a frozen executor, changing its instructions and tools rather than its weights. On circle packing, one campaign improved the sum of radii from 0.960 to 2.541 by round 10; the harness later scored 2.635984 in nine runs with GLM-5.2. This illustrates reuse, not guaranteed transfer.

hot.title: EgoExplorer: A Vision-Motion-Touch Observatory for Human Loco-Manipulation In Situ
hot.summary: EgoExplorer records continuous whole-body activity by combining five wearable trackers, egocentric video, and articulated hand sensing. Its Calibrate-Complete-Constrain pipeline calibrates body shape and tracker mounts, completes unobserved motion with a temporal prior, and refines it using measurement and geometry constraints. On evaluation, error is 18.0 mm versus 64.1 mm for locally fine-tuned AvatarPoser, against tracker-fitted references, not independent ground truth.

hot.title: World Modeling through Spectral Alignment
hot.summary: SpecWM steers a latent world model by training its encoder to match target similarities between observations, rather than relying only on prediction. Temporal similarity uses frame order without physical labels. In simulated tests, both SpecWM variants outperform LeWM in CEM success. On OGBench Scene, temporal SpecWM reaches 77% versus LeWM at 49%; these results establish neither real-world performance nor planning efficiency.

hot.title: Can Learning to Answer Spatial Questions Improve Novel-View Generation?
hot.summary: Ask4NV trains a novel-view generator with 3D question-answering and visual-grounding objectives alongside generation. It conditions generation on camera-aware VAE and ViT features from source views. On DL3DV, matched ViT-conditioned joint training reaches 14.939 PSNR and 0.313 LPIPS, versus 13.878 and 0.384 for generation-only training. Across four evaluated datasets, it leads PSNR, LPIPS, and ATE; these results cover tested benchmarks.

likes.title: Embodied Turing Machines: Stateful Code for Robot Recursive Self-Improvement
likes.summary: COAP represents scene state in code and uses a fixed task program to choose actions, check outcomes, and update its records. At test time, it uses camera images and robot measurements without a model service. On RoboDojo, it reaches 70.24% overall success, versus 31.38% for PhysicalRSI. Results are from simulation and depend on state measurement and code robustness.

likes.title: MiMo-V2.6: Scaling Reinforcement Learning Towards Self-Improvement
likes.summary: The authors train coding agents with groupwise grading, comparing attempts at the same task to add quality signals to binary test rewards. Online Groupwise Advantage Redistribution shifts positive credit toward higher-quality passing patches. MiMo-V2.6-Pro’s reported average pass-rate score across three sampled attempts rises from 58.4 to 72.6 on DeepSWE v1.1, but this mixed-task run does not isolate grading or compute effects.

likes.title: Recursive Self-Improvement through Multi-Agent Self-Supervision
likes.summary: MASS improves open-ended research agents by having model copies coordinate through task-specific workflows, then fine-tuning their shared model on selected orchestrator and subagent trajectories. After two cycles, it achieves 1.2–1.6 times the base model’s score per output token on four research benchmarks. This does not extend to coding benchmarks, where the reported ratios are 0.96 and 0.94.

likes.title: Next-Concept Modeling: Fast, Parallel Coarse-to-Fine Text Generation
likes.summary: NCM generates text by encoding it into hierarchical discrete representations and predicting them coarse to fine, with codes at each level generated in parallel. It reports LM1B generative perplexity of 93.05 at 12 function evaluations, compared with DUO’s 97.30 at 128, alongside similar measured diversity and a reported 21× wall-clock speedup. These results are benchmark-specific, and larger-scale behavior remains open.

likes.title: RSI-Anything: Unlocking Recursive Self-Improvement with World Models
likes.summary: RSI-Anything uses predicted outcomes to select actions for testing, then pairs predictions with observed results to guide policy updates and conditional world-model adaptation. With the coder fixed on CodeContests, hidden-test all-pass success rose from 26.3% with a static verifier to 29.2% with fixed-model selection and 31.2% with adaptation, at similar online test usage. This does not establish sustained joint improvement.

likes.title: LeWAM: End-to-End World and Action Modeling with JEPAs
likes.summary: LeWAM jointly learns how actions change a scene and which actions are plausible, then uses proposed actions to plan manipulation. Its model predicts latent states and action distributions, refining candidate sequences against a goal. Across ten simulated tasks, it averages 93.5% success versus 50.9% for LeWM with CEM. These results concern task-specific goal reaching from offline data, not broad transfer.

likes.title: A Balanced Data Diet: Addressing the Exploration Bottleneck in Mega-Scale RL for Robot Control
likes.summary: Success Guided Sampling (SGS) allocates training episodes across a fixed set of task configurations according to recent success rates, emphasizing situations with intermediate success while retaining nonzero sampling probability for all configurations. In settings, it improves results: Anymal-D locomotion reaches 73% success at 1 million environments, versus 54% with PLR. Hardware nut-and-bolt transfer succeeds in 18 of 48 trials.

likes.title: Correction Training for Diffusion Models
likes.summary: The authors introduce a corrector for diffusion image generation that refines the denoiser’s clean-image prediction before each sampling update. Trained on the denoiser’s own predictions, the corrector can be applied repeatedly. On class-conditional ImageNet-256 with DiT-XL/2 at 250 network evaluations, it lowers FID-50K from 9.58 unguided to 2.07, versus 2.51 for CFG, with lower precision but higher recall than CFG.

likes.title: Can Jev be Your Q or Policy in Reinforcement Learning?
likes.summary: The paper tests frozen Jev as guidance within reinforcement-learning training: as an action reference, exploration judge, and replay rater. Across nine MiniGrid tasks and three Atari games, learners sometimes outperform direct Jev control. Results depend on task and supplied information; in FourRooms, direct Jev succeeds in 96% of episodes with engineered navigation features, versus 40% without them.

likes.title: AgentGarten: Code Worlds for Evolving Agents
likes.summary: AgentGarten separates executable world state and rules from a shared neural renderer that generates agents’ observations from engine-provided geometry. Agents act on rendered first-person views, review outcomes, and carry playbooks into later rounds. In hide-and-seek, agents built shelters by round 4 and used ramps by round 10; these milestones reflect pretrained agents and a different learning setup, so they are not directly comparable.

likes.title: SuperNav: An Agentic Navigation System for Any Task in Any Scene
likes.summary: SuperNav uses a pretrained multimodal large language model (MLLM) to navigate environments across single-object, ordered multi-object, and demand-driven tasks. A harness provides tools, reusable Skills, task state, and context management; the model selects destinations while an executor handles motion. On 150 Habitat-GS single-object tasks, its Geo-based Executor achieves 78.00% success versus UniNaVid's 34.00%, supporting the complete system only in tested settings.

likes.title: Prior or Feedback? What an LLM Uses When Adapting Neural Operators
likes.summary: The authors test LLM tuning of a Fourier neural operator (FNO) using hosted DeepSeek-V4 Pro over 20 trials. It achieves lower held-out test nRMSE in all 36 runs against random search and 35 of 36 against TPE. Its first proposal beats 91.7% of random configurations; replay shows choices respond to score assignments, but not that feedback improves test performance.

likes.title: ReplaySSM: Cache SSM Inputs, Not State
likes.summary: ReplaySSM reduces recurrent-state writes during state-space model decoding by keeping a checkpoint and buffering recent inputs, then periodically folding them into the checkpoint. It also supports pointer-based speculative rollback and separate low- and high-precision checkpoints. At batch size 256, whole-model decode latency improved 1.20–1.47× across four hybrid models; gains depend on setup and batch size, and checkpoint reads remain.

likes.title: TokenRouter: Efficient Serving System for Token-Level LLM Routing
likes.summary: TokenRouter serves inference with per-token routing between language models, using asynchronous subservers and delayed batch admission. Developers define routing and state handoffs; each model server buffers arrivals and uses a throughput model to select a threshold. On R2R’s AIME setup at concurrency 4, it reports 244.56 generated tokens/s versus 89.62 for official R2R, a serving-efficiency result under routing assumptions.

likes.title: Vela: User Behavior as Supervision Sparks LLM Intelligence
likes.summary: Vela turns users’ timestamped behavior histories into supervision for predicting future actions and answering rubric-scored questions grounded in past evidence. It separates visible history from future outcomes to avoid leaking prediction targets. Fine-tuning Qwen3.6-35B-A3B on Vela-Instruct raises VelaBench from 51.5 to 63.0, but this shows gains after training on behavior-derived data, not that behavior supervision alone caused them.

likes.title: Thinking Inertia: LLMs Keep Thinking When Told Not To
likes.summary: The authors measure whether language models give answer-only responses by separating visible pre-answer text from final answers. They assess strict compliance, relevance, and explicit inference separately from accuracy. In matched numeric questions, changing multiple-choice to open-ended reduced Qwen3-32B accuracy from 77.8% to 52.6% and raised explicit inference from 86.95% to 90.14%. This measures visible output, not hidden computation.

likes.title: BrickBench: Evaluating Agentic Brick Design
likes.summary: BrickBench evaluates whether coding agents can turn written prompts into LEGO assemblies that meet construction checks and depict the requested scene. In BrickAgent, agents select parts, place them through compatible connectors, render builds, and revise them using validation feedback. GPT-6 Astra scores 1.00 on overall validity and 0.954 on VQA, but stability is simulated and does not establish real-world strength.

likes.title: Dino Forcing Flow Models: Do not denoise what you can predict
likes.summary: DINO Forcing uses a pretrained DINO vision encoder to guide image generation without separately denoising a feature stream. From a noisy image, it predicts DINO features and reuses them as conditioning, with feature alignment during training. On ImageNet, it reports unguided FID 2.47 after 100 latent-space epochs and 5.53 after 200 pixel-space epochs; these comparisons are benchmark-specific, not wall-clock evidence.

likes.title: Few-Step Generation via Data-Space Iteration
likes.summary: The authors introduce data-space iteration for few-step image generation, passing a draft between calls while retaining the original noise input instead of following a preset generation-time noise schedule. The method keeps DMD self-rollout training, which still uses noise time. On guided class-conditional ImageNet 256×256 at four NFE, it reports FID 2.29 versus 2.37 for the best of three flow-map schedules.

likes.title: MagicBeanStalk: Escaping the RLVR Zero Advantage Trap with Recursive Data Synthesis
likes.summary: MagicBeanStalk uses verified solutions to build math problems preserving targeted reasoning, then screens them for mixed outcomes under a target policy and response budget. In a 78,000-problem corpus, about 88% were all-correct or all-incorrect across eight gpt-oss-120b rollouts at 32K. For gpt-oss-120b, training raised average pass@1 across eight benchmarks from 61.2% to 69.8% at 16K.
